items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: The interviewee only responds with 'Mmm.' to the interviewer's statement about Karl Berger; no personal interaction or relationship is described.

ctx.x: Ooo. That’s a great question. I suppose something singable, and in fact a lot of the time when I’m writing I’m singing the line rather than necessarily playing it on the piano or the saxophone. Or I might start there and then I think oh well what comes next. Or sing what I’ve just written and then see what voice comes up then. So I suppose that’s part of it. Being singable. But it’s so intangible, some of this stuff, the quest for the perfect melody. I will answer that from a spiritual perspective actually,…

Well Karl Berger, who passed away a couple of years ago, but he had the Creative Music Workshop north of New York. And he said, “Music is being thought of as something that entertains us and that can be used for other certain purposes. But it’s a world. You go there. Everybody can go there whether you play or not. You’re in the world of spontaneity and you’re no longer in the thinking world. You leave the thinking world behind.
